frs_sections.title: SCOPE AND OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

This document defines the DDR4 SDRAM (Double Data Rate Fourth-generation
Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory) standard, JEDEC Standard
JESD79-4. DDR4 is the mainstream commodity main-memory DRAM generation
that succeeds DDR3 (JESD79-3) and precedes DDR5 (JESD79-5).

A DDR4 SDRAM is a high-speed, clocked, double-data-rate dynamic memory.
Commands and addresses are captured on the rising edge of the
differential clock CK_t/CK_c; data DQ is transferred on both edges of
the differential data strobe DQS_t/DQS_c (double data rate). DDR4
defines a single 64-bit data channel per DIMM (72-bit with ECC). DDR4
devices are offered as x4, x8, and x16 organizations.

frs_sections.title: SINGLE-CHANNEL ORGANIZATION
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 defines a SINGLE data channel per module. A standard DDR4 UDIMM /
RDIMM presents one 64-bit-wide data path (DQ[63:0]); an ECC module
presents 72 bits (64 data + 8 ECC). This is the defining organizational
difference from DDR5, which splits the module into two independent
32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels. DDR4 has NO sub-channel split: a
single command/address bus drives the full 64-bit data width.

Per-device data widths:
  - x4  : DQ[3:0],  one DQS_t/DQS_c pair per device.
  - x8  : DQ[7:0],  one DQS_t/DQS_c pair, one DM_n/DBI_n.
  - x16 : DQ[15:0], two DQS pairs (lower/upper byte), two DM_n/DBI_n.

==================================================================

frs_sections.title: SUPPLY VOLTAGE
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 operates at:
  VDD  = 1.2 V (core)
  VDDQ = 1.2 V (DQ I/O)
  VPP  = 2.5 V (DRAM activating / wordline pump supply, new in DDR4)
  VREFCA externally supplied; VREFDQ generated INTERNALLY (on-die) and
         set by VrefDQ training (a DDR4 feature — DDR3 used an external
         VREFDQ).

The 1.2 V VDD/VDDQ rail is a primary DDR4 discriminator versus DDR3's
1.5 V rail.

==================================================================

frs_sections.title: BANK GROUPS AND BANK ORGANIZATION
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 introduces BANK GROUPS, a new addressing hierarchy not present in
DDR3. The banks of a DDR4 device are partitioned into bank groups:

  - x4 and x8 devices : 4 bank groups, each with 4 banks = 16 banks.
  - x16 devices       : 2 bank groups, each with 4 banks = 8 banks.

Bank group address pins:
  - BG0, BG1 select the bank group (x4/x8: BG0/BG1; x16: BG0 only).
  - BA0, BA1 select the bank within the bank group.

Bank groups exist so that consecutive accesses to DIFFERENT bank groups
can run back-to-back at the short column-to-column delay tCCD_S (CCD
short), while accesses WITHIN the SAME bank group incur the longer
tCCD_L (CCD long). This bank-group timing split (tCCD_S vs tCCD_L,
tRRD_S vs tRRD_L, tWTR_S vs tWTR_L…

frs_sections.title: GEAR-DOWN MODE
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 defines GEAR-DOWN MODE, programmable via Mode Register MR3. In the
default 1/1-rate (full-rate) mode, command/address is sampled on every
rising CK edge. In GEAR-DOWN (1/2-rate) mode, the command/address bus is
sampled on every OTHER rising clock edge, halving the effective CA
capture rate to ease command-bus timing at the highest DDR4 speed bins.
Gear-down requires a defined synchronization (Sync) pulse to align the
controller and DRAM to the same 1/2-rate command phase. Gear-down mode
is a DDR4 feature introduced in JESD79-4.

frs_sections.title: VREFDQ INTERNAL GENERATION AND TRAINING
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 moves the DQ reference voltage (VREFDQ) ON-DIE. Each DDR4 SDRAM
generates its own VREFDQ internally, programmable over a defined range
in fine steps via Mode Register MR6. The controller runs a VREFDQ
TRAINING sequence (VrefDQ training), entered through MR6, to center the
internal DQ reference within the data eye for each device. The DRAM
provides a VREF training range select (Range 1 / Range 2) and a step
adjust. On-die VREFDQ with controller-directed training is a DDR4
feature; DDR3 used an externally supplied VREFDQ.

frs_sections.title: SPEED BINS
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 speed bins (data rate in MT/s, double the CK frequency):
  DDR4-1600  (CK 800 MHz)
  DDR4-1866
  DDR4-2133
  DDR4-2400
  DDR4-2666
  DDR4-2933
  DDR4-3200  (CK 1600 MHz)

DDR4 is a DLL-based SDRAM: an on-die Delay-Locked Loop aligns the output
DQS/DQ to the input clock CK. Each speed bin defines CL (CAS latency),
tRCD, tRP, and tRAS in the speed-bin tables. The data rate is twice the
CK rate because DQ is transferred on both clock/strobe edges (double
data rate).

frs_sections.title: COMMAND TRUTH TABLE
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 multiplexes the legacy RAS_n / CAS_n / WE_n function pins with high
address bits and adds the ACT_n (Activate) pin:

  Pin       DDR4 dual function
  ACT_n     Activate command flag (LOW = ACTIVATE).
  RAS_n/A16 RAS_n when ACT_n LOW; address A16 when ACT_n HIGH.
  CAS_n/A15 CAS_n when ACT_n LOW; address A15 when ACT_n HIGH.
  WE_n/A14  WE_n  when ACT_n LOW; address A14 when ACT_n HIGH.

Command encoding (CKE, CS_n, ACT_n, RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14):

  ACTIVATE (ACT)  : ACT_n=L, opens a row in a bank (bank group BG, bank
                    BA, row address). Timing tRCD before column access.
  READ (RD)       : ACT_n=H, RAS_n=H, CAS_n=L, WE_n=H. Column read; CL
                    later, DQ burst on DQS edges.

frs_sections.title: KEY TIMING PARAMETERS
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

  tRCD  : ACTIVATE-to-READ/WRITE (RAS-to-CAS) delay.
  tRP   : PRECHARGE period.
  tRAS  : ACTIVATE-to-PRECHARGE (row active time).
  tRC   : tRAS + tRP (ACTIVATE-to-ACTIVATE same bank).
  tRFC  : REFRESH-to-ACTIVATE / REFRESH cycle time.
  tWR   : WRITE recovery time.
  tCCD_S: column-to-column delay, different bank group (CCD short).
  tCCD_L: column-to-column delay, same bank group (CCD long).
  tRRD_S/tRRD_L : ACTIVATE-to-ACTIVATE delay (different / same bank group).
  tWTR_S/tWTR_L : WRITE-to-READ turnaround (different / same bank group).
  tFAW  : four-activate window.
  tREFI : average refresh interval (7.8 us at <=85 C, 3.9 us above).
  CL/CWL: read / write CAS latency (from the speed-bin tables).

frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

  CK_t, CK_c        : differential input clock.
  CKE               : clock enable (power-down / self-refresh control).
  CS_n              : chip select (per rank).
  ACT_n             : activate command flag.
  RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14 : multiplexed command / high address.
  A[13:0]           : address bus (row / column).
  A10/AP            : auto-precharge / precharge-all.
  A12/BC_n          : burst chop on-the-fly select.
  BG0, BG1          : bank group address.
  BA0, BA1          : bank address.
  DQ[3:0] / [7:0] / [15:0] : bidirectional data (x4/x8/x16).
  DQS_t, DQS_c      : differential bidirectional data strobe (per byte).

frs_sections.title: REFRESH AND LOW POWER
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 supports:
  - All-bank and per-bank REFRESH.
  - Fine Granularity Refresh (1x / 2x / 4x) trading tRFC for tREFI.
  - Self-Refresh (CKE LOW + command), with Auto Self-Refresh (ASR) and
    temperature-controlled / low-power self-refresh ranges.
  - Precharge power-down and active power-down (CKE LOW).
  - Maximum Power Saving Mode (MR4) for deep idle.

==================================================================

frs_sections.title: DISTINCTION FROM SIBLING MEMORY STANDARDS
frs_sections.content:
==================================================================

DDR4 (this document, JESD79-4) is distinguished from:

  - DDR3 (JESD79-3): DDR3 runs at 1.5 V, has NO bank groups (8 banks via
    BA0..BA2 only), NO gear-down mode, NO write CRC, NO CA parity, NO
    on-die VREFDQ, and uses an external VREFDQ. DDR4 adds all of these.

  - The next DRAM generation (the JESD79 fifth-generation standard):
    that generation splits the module into two narrower independent
    sub-channels and adds receiver equalization, on-die error correction,
    and an on-module power-management device with an SPD hub at a lower
    rail. DDR4 instead presents a SINGLE 64-bit channel at 1.2 V with one
    command/address bus driving the full data width. This document does
    NOT define a sub-channel spl…

protocol_overview.type: Clocked, double-data-rate, bank-organized synchronous DRAM (JEDEC JESD79-4). A single 64-bit (72-bit ECC) channel; commands/addresses captured on the rising CK edge; data on both DQS edges.
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex on DQ (read or write, not both simultaneously); command/address/clock is unidirectional controller → SDRAM
protocol_overview.ddr_signaling: Data (DQ) and data-mask (DM) are sampled on both edges of DQS (double data rate). Command/address/control/clock-enable are sampled on the rising edge of CK only (single data rate).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Bus master. Drives CK/CK#, CKE, CS#, ODT, RAS#/CAS#/WE#, BA[2:0], A[15:0], DM, RESET#. Sources DQ + DQS + DM on write; sinks DQ + DQS on read. Implements scheduling.
protocol_overview.sdram_role: Bus slave. Decodes RAS/CAS/WE/CS into commands per Command Truth Table. Drives DQ + DQS on read; sinks DQ + DQS on write. Generates internal refresh in SELF REFRESH; tracks ODT.

data_strobe: DQS, DQS# (differential, bidirectional; DQSL/DQSU for x16)
data_mask: DM (write data mask; DMU/DML for x16)

protocol_overview.clocking: Source-synchronous: a forwarded differential clock CK_t/CK_c carries commands; a forwarded differential data strobe DQS_t/DQS_c carries data (double data rate). An on-die DLL aligns output DQS/DQ to CK.
new_vs_ddr3: Bank Groups (BG0/BG1) with short/long timings (tCCD_S/L, tRRD_S/L, tWTR_S/L).
Write CRC on the data bus + ALERT_n.
1.2 V VDD/VDDQ (vs 1.5 V); VPP 2.5 V; Rtt_PARK.
ACT_n command flag with multiplexed RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14.

compliance_requirements: Single 64-bit (72-bit ECC) channel at 1.2 V; x4/x8/x16.
Bank Groups with short/long bank-group timings.
Gear-down mode, Data Bus Inversion, on-die VrefDQ training.
Write CRC and CA parity, both reported on ALERT_n.
ACT_n command truth table (RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14).
BL8 / BC4 (on-the-fly) bursts; MR0..MR6 mode registers.
ODT Rtt_Nom / Rtt_WR / Rtt_PARK; ZQ calibration against RZQ.

auto_cited_sections.heading: RDIMM / LRDIMM: RCD AND DATA BUFFER

error_response_conditions: Write CRC error — signaled on ALERT_n; the write is not committed and is retried.
CA parity error — the command is blocked and ALERT_n is asserted for the CA-parity error window (persistent error mode).
Connectivity / boundary-scan error — reported via ALERT_n.
Refresh / timing violation — data integrity not guaranteed if tREFI/tRFC are violated.

functional_requirements.text: DDR4 presents a single 64-bit (72-bit ECC) data channel per module; there is no sub-channel split. Devices are x4/x8/x16.
Commands and addresses are captured on the rising edge of the differential clock CK_t/CK_c; data DQ is transferred on both edges of the differential strobe DQS_t/DQS_c (double data rate).
DDR4 operates at VDD = VDDQ = 1.2 V with VPP = 2.5 V; VREFCA is supplied externally and VREFDQ is generated internally (on-die).

The banks are partitioned into Bank Groups (BG0/BG1): x4/x8 = 4 bank groups x 4 banks = 16 banks; x16 = 2 bank groups x 4 banks = 8 banks. Accesses to different bank groups use tCCD_S (short); same-bank-group accesses use tCCD_L (long).
Gear-down mode (MR3) samples command/address on every other rising CK edge (1/2 rate) with a synchronization pulse, to ease command-bus timing at high speed bins.
Data Bus Inversion (MR5) repurposes DM_n as DBI_n per byte to minimize DQ lines driven LOW; DM and write-DBI are mutually exclusive on the shared pin.
Each DDR4 SDRAM generates VREFDQ on-die (programmable in fine steps via MR6) and the controller runs a VrefDQ training sequence (Range 1 / Range 2) to center the DQ reference.
Write CRC (MR2) appends an 8-bit CRC to each BL8 write burst; a detected CRC error is signaled on ALERT_n and the write is not committed (controller retries).
Command/Address parity (PAR pin, MR5) covers the command and address inputs; a parity error blocks the command and asserts ALERT_n for the programmed CA-parity error window.

The command truth table uses the ACT_n flag: when ACT_n is LOW the command is ACTIVATE; when ACT_n is HIGH, RAS_n/A16, CAS_n/A15, WE_n/A14 encode READ/WRITE/PRECHARGE/REFRESH/MRS and carry high address bits.
Data is transferred in bursts of BL8 (eight beats) or BC4 (burst chop of four); A12/BC_n selects BL8 vs BC4 on-the-fly per command. Mode registers MR0..MR6 are written via MRS.
On-die termination supports Rtt_Nom (MR1), Rtt_WR (MR2), and Rtt_PARK (MR5, new in DDR4); ZQ calibration (ZQCL/ZQCS) calibrates the output driver and ODT against the external RZQ (240 ohm) resistor.
DDR4 supports all-bank and per-bank REFRESH, Fine Granularity Refresh (1x/2x/4x), self-refresh with Auto Self-Refresh (ASR), and power-down / Maximum Power Saving Mode.

configurations.name: Burst length 8 fixed (BL8)
configurations.description: MR0 A[1:0] = 00. Every READ/WRITE is an 8-beat burst on DQ.

configurations.name: Burst chop 4 / burst length 8 on-the-fly
configurations.description: MR0 A[1:0] = 01. A12/BC# during READ/WRITE selects BC4 (A12=L) or BL8 (A12=H).

configurations.name: Burst chop 4 fixed (BC4)
configurations.description: MR0 A[1:0] = 10. Every READ/WRITE is a 4-beat chopped burst.

configurations.name: DLL on (normal operation)
configurations.description: MR1 A0 = 0; DLL provides synchronous DQS/DQ output timing relative to CK.

configurations.name: DLL off (optional low-frequency / test)
configurations.description: MR1 A0 = 1; only CL=6 and CWL=6 supported.

configurations.name: Active Power-Down (APD)
configurations.description: CKE LOW with at least one bank active; tXP to exit; DLL kept enabled.

configurations.name: Precharge Power-Down Fast Exit
configurations.description: CKE LOW with all banks precharged and MR0 A12=1; tXP exit.

configurations.name: Precharge Power-Down Slow Exit
configurations.description: CKE LOW with all banks precharged and MR0 A12=0; tXPDLL exit.

configurations.name: Self-Refresh Extended Temperature Range
configurations.description: 0–95 °C; possibly doubled refresh rate via SRT (MR2 A7) or ASR (MR2 A6).

configurations.name: Write Leveling Mode
configurations.description: MR1 A7=1; DQ becomes feedback path for CK/CK# sampling by DQS.

configurations.name: MPR Read mode
configurations.description: MR3 A2=1; READ returns predefined pattern instead of array data.
